+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess,tempfile,json,hashlib,shutil,sys
+root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+repo=root.parents[3]
+out=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="controls-",dir=root/"evidence"))
+sha=lambda b:hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+paths=[root/"layout.mjs",root/"render.mjs",repo/"src/ui/referenceMapView.ts",root/"board.json",root/"map.svg",root/"preview.html"]
+original={p:p.read_bytes() for p in paths}
+for p,b in original.items():
+ dest=out/"originals"/p.relative_to(repo);dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);dest.write_bytes(b)
+shutil.copy2(__file__,out/"script-input.py")
+layout=original[root/"layout.mjs"].decode()
+ending=" board.routes=routed;\n return board;"
+assert layout.count(ending)==1
+tail=lambda code:layout.replace(ending," board.routes=routed;\n "+code+"\n return board;")
+view=original[repo/"src/ui/referenceMapView.ts"].decode()
+star='x:Number(n.querySelector(".count")!.getAttribute("x"))-25,y:Number(n.querySelector(".count")!.getAttribute("y"))-28'
+assert view.count(star)==1
+render=original[root/"render.mjs"].decode()
+start=render.index("export function svg(board){");end=render.index("export const html=",start)
+quiet='\n.country .name{font-size:9px;font-weight:400;stroke:none}.country:is(:hover,:focus,.selected) .name{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;stroke:#f8f2e2;stroke-width:1.5}</style>'
+raw_caption=render[:start]+"export const svg=board=>inheritedSvg(board).replace('</style>',"+json.dumps(quiet)+");\n"+render[end:]
+cases=[
+ ("coast-identity",root/"layout.mjs","export const coastPostprocess=input=>structuredClone(input);\n","unit",False),
+ ("graph-metadata",root/"layout.mjs",tail("board.provinces[0].borders=[];"),"unit",False),
+ ("capture-port-inland",root/"layout.mjs",tail("board.routes[0].points[0]=[...board.provinces.find(p=>p.id===board.routes[0].from).labelAt];"),"unit",False),
+ ("label-outside-country",root/"layout.mjs",tail("board.provinces[0].labelAt=[...board.islands.find(i=>i.id===board.provinces[0].island).polygon[0]];"),"unit",False),
+ ("stateful-construction","layout", "let mutationCalls=0;\n"+tail("board.provinces[0].polygon[0][0]+=(++mutationCalls%2)/1024;"),"unit",False),
+ ("old-painted-map",repo/"src/ui/referenceMapView.ts",view.replace("T64/map.svg?raw","T63/map.svg?raw"),"playable",False),
+ ("canonical-star-positions",repo/"src/ui/referenceMapView.ts",view.replace(star,'x:_map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id)!.labelAt[0]-25,y:_map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id)!.labelAt[1]-10'),"playable",False),
+ ("caption-reservations",root/"render.mjs",raw_caption,"browser",True),
+]
+rows=[]
+for name,p,mutant,kind,rebuild in cases:
+ if len(sys.argv)>1 and name not in sys.argv[1:]:continue
+ if p=="layout":p=root/"layout.mjs"
+ case=out/name;case.mkdir();(case/"mutated-source.txt").write_text(mutant)
+ row={"name":name,"path":str(p.relative_to(repo)),"originalSha256":sha(original[p]),"mutatedSha256":sha(mutant.encode())}
+ try:
+  p.write_text(mutant)
+  if rebuild:
+   generated=case/"regenerated"
+   with (case/"build.txt").open("wb") as log:build=subprocess.run(["node",str(root/"construct.mjs"),str(generated)],cwd=repo,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
+   row["rebuildExit"]=build.returncode
+   if build.returncode:raise RuntimeError("Mutant did not regenerate; not a behavioral negative")
+   for asset_name in ["board.json","map.svg","preview.html"]:shutil.copy2(generated/asset_name,root/asset_name)
+  command=["python3",str(root/"checks.py"),"--focused"] if kind=="unit" else ["python3",str(root/"run.py")]+(["--grep","playable geography"] if kind=="playable" else [])
+  with (case/"output.txt").open("wb") as log:result=subprocess.run(command,cwd=repo,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
+  row.update(command=command,exit=result.returncode)
+  text=(case/"output.txt").read_text();report=json.loads(text)
+  produced=repo/report["output"]
+  negative=(produced/"0.txt").read_text() if kind=="unit" else (produced/"raw/output.txt").read_text()
+  row["evidence"]=str(produced.relative_to(repo))
+  row["assertionNegative"]=result.returncode!=0 and any(token in negative for token in ["AssertionError","expect(received)","Expected:"])
+ except Exception as error:row.update(assertionNegative=False,error=repr(error))
+ finally:
+  for target,b in original.items():target.write_bytes(b)
+  row["restored"]=all(target.read_bytes()==b for target,b in original.items())
+  rows.append(row)
+  (out/"report.json").write_text(json.dumps({"cases":rows,"allRestored":all(r["restored"] for r in rows)},indent=2)+"\n")
+print(json.dumps({"output":str(out.relative_to(repo)),"cases":rows},indent=2))
+assert rows and all(r["assertionNegative"] and r["restored"] for r in rows)

+ ("graph-metadata",root/"layout.mjs",tail("board.provinces[0].borders=[];"),"unit",False),
+ ("capture-port-inland",root/"layout.mjs",tail("board.routes[0].points[0]=[...board.provinces.find(p=>p.id===board.routes[0].from).labelAt];"),"unit",False),
+ ("label-outside-country",root/"layout.mjs",tail("board.provinces[0].labelAt=[...board.islands.find(i=>i.id===board.provinces[0].island).polygon[0]];"),"unit",False),
+ ("stateful-construction","layout", "let mutationCalls=0;\n"+tail("board.provinces[0].polygon[0][0]+=(++mutationCalls%2)/1024;"),"unit",False),
+ ("old-painted-map",repo/"src/ui/referenceMapView.ts",view.replace("T64/map.svg?raw","T63/map.svg?raw"),"playable",False),
+ ("canonical-star-positions",repo/"src/ui/referenceMapView.ts",view.replace(star,'x:_map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id)!.labelAt[0]-25,y:_map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id)!.labelAt[1]-10'),"playable",False),

+]
+rows=[]
+for name,p,mutant,kind,rebuild in cases:
+ if len(sys.argv)>1 and name not in sys.argv[1:]:continue
+ if p=="layout":p=root/"layout.mjs"
+ case=out/name;case.mkdir();(case/"mutated-source.txt").write_text(mutant)
+ row={"name":name,"path":str(p.relative_to(repo)),"originalSha256":sha(original[p]),"mutatedSha256":sha(mutant.encode())}
+ try:
+  p.write_text(mutant)

+ ("canonical-star-positions",repo/"src/ui/referenceMapView.ts",view.replace(star,'x:_map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id)!.labelAt[0]-25,y:_map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id)!.labelAt[1]-10'),"playable",False),
+ ("caption-reservations",root/"render.mjs",raw_caption,"browser",True),
+]

+ if p=="layout":p=root/"layout.mjs"
+ case=out/name;case.mkdir();(case/"mutated-source.txt").write_text(mutant)
+ row={"name":name,"path":str(p.relative_to(repo)),"originalSha256":sha(original[p]),"mutatedSha256":sha(mutant.encode())}
+ try:
+  p.write_text(mutant)
+  if rebuild:

+   row["rebuildExit"]=build.returncode

+   for asset_name in ["board.json","map.svg","preview.html"]:shutil.copy2(generated/asset_name,root/asset_name)

+  with (case/"output.txt").open("wb") as log:result=subprocess.run(command,cwd=repo,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
+  row.update(command=command,exit=result.returncode)
+  text=(case/"output.txt").read_text();report=json.loads(text)
+  produced=repo/report["output"]
+  negative=(produced/"0.txt").read_text() if kind=="unit" else (produced/"raw/output.txt").read_text()
+  row["evidence"]=str(produced.relative_to(repo))
+  row["assertionNegative"]=result.returncode!=0 and any(token in negative for token in ["AssertionError","expect(received)","Expected:"])
+ except Exception as error:row.update(assertionNegative=False,error=repr(error))
+ finally:
+  for target,b in original.items():target.write_bytes(b)
+  row["restored"]=all(target.read_bytes()==b for target,b in original.items())
+  rows.append(row)
+  (out/"report.json").write_text(json.dumps({"cases":rows,"allRestored":all(r["restored"] for r in rows)},indent=2)+"\n")
+print(json.dumps({"output":str(out.relative_to(repo)),"cases":rows},indent=2))
+assert rows and all(r["assertionNegative"] and r["restored"] for r in rows)

# Geographical fixed-reference drawing — T64 / issue111

The reference interface uses an original geographical drawing following the direction approved in [T22/#66](https://github.com/diegoami/malpaco/pull/67#issuecomment-6209845674). The owner explicitly allowed visual countries, label anchors, ports and route shapes to move. The current 61 land/15 sea graph,46 country identities,9 islands, bonuses, canonical T63 engine map, ordered deals and saves remain unchanged. T22G proposed a different graph; its topology is not imported.

`layout.mjs` is a pure deterministic construction from the canonical T63 board. It uses the existing outer country cycle and shared graph-face vertices to build coherent subdivisions, with seeded coast variation and exact shared coordinates. The ten-country ladder retains a bent broad-cell subdivision so its hit areas stay usable. Dyadic1/1024 coordinates avoid numerical residuals without changing the existing geometry assertions. These are original [designed] presentation choices developed in the retained probes. Generated-board integration belongs to T36; shared-border curvature belongs to T65.

Country labels reserve the existing 40px hit square and 44px Euclidean spacing. Native measurement found 45-unit emphasized label bounds; 47 vertical/44 horizontal separation accounts for 20-unit product badges and 1 unit clearance. `render.mjs` places island captions in water, outside route strokes, and gives the standalone prototype the existing quiet/emphasized name hierarchy. Actual browser bounds, hit tests and all 46 selected countries protect this independently. Production stars use drawing anchors; saves retain canonical T63 coordinates.

`board.json`, `map.svg` and self-contained `preview.html` are generated assets. The application imports only the SVG; expensive construction does not run during play. Main intentionally amended only reference painted-geometry/route expectations and two opening goldens. Their exact originals are retained in `originals/`; every semantic, replay, fit, timing and other existing assertion stays unchanged.

Reproduce with the established pinned Playwright 1.63.0-noble image/read-only shared dependencies:
```sh
node docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/construct.mjs --check
python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/checks.py --focused
python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/checks.py
python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/run.py
COAST_COMPATIBILITY=1 python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/run.py
python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/inheritance.py
python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/controls.py
```
`construct.mjs [fresh-output-directory]` preserves generated files, exact construction inputs and hashes; it refuses an existing explicit output. With no argument it creates a fresh evidence directory. `--check` compares all three installed assets exactly. No golden update is part of these commands. Browser runs preserve source/raw archives, member hashes, exits and input-stability checks; final unit checks archive project source/test inputs. `index.py` hashes nonraw evidence/deliverables; raw directories remain local with complete compressed originals. Ignore generated Python bytecode only.

Retained evidence landmarks:

| Evidence | What it establishes |
| --- | --- |
| `feasibility-baseline.json` | Immutable T63 passes the unchanged T62 contract. |
| `shape-probe-*`, `geography-probe-*`, `tutte-probe-*`, `dual-probe-*` | Every accepted/rejected shape, actual failures, exact scripts and native captures; chronological explanation retained in `evidence/README-before-production-summary.md`. |
| `checks-q7lynffn`, `run-b6bhqjou` | Identity fails the new coastline assertion;4invariants already hold. Old actual renderer fails atbothdesktop sizes; standalone artifact is absent. Earlier JSON-loader failure `run-hs4c0g2s` is infrastructure, not a behavioral proof. |
| `mock-preflight-xs4xoemy` | Disposable5focused/588fullunits/build/8browser positive; all5temporary source/asset paths restore exactly. |
| `run-1fd1lbm6`, `run-qj68usrq`, `run-osz33r8n`, `run-mq0mq4rh` | Native on-land caption and opening/selected label failures retained without weakening the guards. |
| `label-diagnose-OCKjAe`, `dual-probe-pBNspT`, `run-gbtg5_5g` | Measured emphasized glyph bounds, corrected layout, allunchangedT62constraints, final disposable8/8browser proof with exact restoration. Old technical paint targets are retained under `acceptance/board-before-*`. |
| `checks-b4_j8vjo`, `build-H3ndEH`, `checks-toehrisd` | Real pure constructor matches the locked candidate; generated assets reproduce;588units/build/whitespace pass. |
| `run-1omrt5d_` | Intentional regeneration of only the2declared reference opening goldens; source-stability flag correctly records those writes. Initial missing compatibility selector `run-f2_b0xmu` retained. |
| `run-9lsg_1fb` | 82/82affected pinned cases on stable recorded inputs, including both541-action complete games, direct attacks, save/load, computer gates and readability. |
| `inheritance-hjpzemxt` | 451inherited files; only the renderer, declared paint expectations and2goldens differ. T22/T63/core/other tests remain exact. |
| `controls-1332g1ae` | Eight actual-source assertion negatives: identity, graph metadata, inland port, invalid label, stateful construction, old paint, old star positions and caption reservation deletion. All6source/asset files restore exactly. Caption control regenerates fresh assets before testing. |

The matched full views, T22 reference and coast close-ups support owner judgment. Automated geometry/input checks do not establish appearance or pacing approval; the owner judges the T33 milestone after the requested coastline and border pass.

Final production receipts: `checks-5dytkdwr` passes 588 units/build/whitespace after mutation restoration; its archived inputs and output hashes match. `run-238x6nzl` passes 8 final browser cases with matched full views/close-ups and exact current input hashes. `run-1fmrg5u8` passes 2 direct-input cases after forwarding `ATTACK_EVIDENCE_DIR` into each fresh raw archive. The earlier82-case run predates only that output-routing fix and additional close-up capture calls; runtime/assertions are identical. Its 148 direct captures/saves fell into the inherited suite’s `screenshots` fallback, all within that run’s recorded time window; exact originals remain and are archived/hash-verified under `compatibility-direct-captures-gftxlp99`. `integrity-syidvi9d` verifies current final sources, source/raw archive members, unit outputs and the two declared compatibility-only input differences. `previews/provenance.json` records 38 unchanged PNG copies and their exact source paths/hashes.

Coverage completion: `run-4elvj6jz` passes8additional existing accessibility/friendly-feedback cases, with source/raw archives and current inputs verified. The combined affected set is82+8cases; the compatibility selector now includes those two suites, and independent review runs all90 together. That is the only later configuration difference from the final eight-case/route-smoke manifests; their default selection, runtime and assertions are unchanged. The earlier integrity record applies at its recorded checkpoint; `coverage-integrity-*` documents this bounded selection expansion. No additional CI run was started.

# T64 Natural coastline postprocessing

- **Kind**: slice
- **Issue**: #111 · **Branch**: `task/T64-natural-coastlines` · **Merge after**: T63 and #138.
- **Difficulty**: Hard; coast detail must preserve every protected landing and usable region.
- **Implementer**: owner-selected main session, isolated worktree; main preflight and recorded contract required.
- **Reviewer**: owner-selected MiniMax M3 via OpenCode; independent family, live ID required.
- **Evidence**: owner selected A; on 2026-10-17 explicitly required coastline/border polish before another presentation, superseding the deferral. Owner additionally selected recovery of #66/T22’s approved geographical direction, allowing visual country/label positions, ports and route shapes to move while preserving gameplay connections and saves. T60 constraints and adopted T62/T63 safety reservations remain binding; their absolute coordinates are no longer fixed.
- **Owns**: src/ui/**; tests/ui/**; tests/e2e/**; docs/prototypes/new-game/T64/**; current-reference notes in docs/spike.md; append-only RUN-NOTES.md.
- **Scope**: Recover #66/T22’s approved geographical direction in the fixed-reference playable map with an original deterministic layout and coastline treatment. Generated-board integration follows under T36; it no longer delays this reference presentation pass. Visual country positions, label anchors, port positions and route shapes may change; rebuild valid landing zones and water corridors at their new positions. Update each island silhouette and its outer country boundaries consistently, retaining exact current adjacency, connected cells, full label/hit reservations and selectable rendered regions. Keep engine map/save identities byte-exact: relocated drawing geometry is presentation only. Coherent subdivision may move with layout; canonical shared-border naturalization is T65; terrain decoration is #119. No game-rule, income or generator-distribution changes.
- **Done when**:
  1. `npx vitest run tests/ui/coast-postprocess.test.ts` — identical inputs/seed reproduce output; exact current graph, shared boundaries, coast attachment, rebuilt reserved corridors, label/hit areas and valid subdivision remain intact across the retained corpus.
  2. `npx playwright test tests/e2e/coast-postprocess.spec.ts` — rendered coast geometry is painted and selectable in a standalone view at 800×540, 1280×800 and 1920×1080, plus actual playable input at both supported desktop sizes; actual labels and routes remain clear; save matched before/after full views and close-ups for owner judgment.
  3. `npm test`, `npm run build` and `git diff --check` pass; affected pinned browser suites pass; retain all drafts, failures, measured outputs and hashes.
- **Hazards**: Main preflights commands before dispatch and splits further if the work exceeds one run. Do not jitter independent polygon copies or turn decorative coves into topology changes. Automated checks protect geometry; matched views include approved T22 G as the visual reference. Owner judges geographical coherence, naturalness and clutter. No automatic approval follows from passing constraints. This presentation pass is an owner-required prerequisite to the next T33 presentation. Keep T22 G and T63 source fixtures immutable; intentionally amend reference-only painted-geometry expectations/goldens with originals retained and the reason declared, never weaken topology/fit/replay assertions.

## Implementer contract

You implement <T<nn>>. The task file above is the contract.
- Build only what the task asks for, even inside a file it requires; say why for each changed file. (L44)
- A Done-when you cannot meet: stop and report. Never weaken an assertion, skip a test or edit the task file.
- **Constraint-feasibility probe** (when the task names structural constraints and a target success
  rate): before any algorithmic change, run a small smoke test that confirms the constraint
  set alone is feasible at the target rate (often a wide-seed sweep of the existing generator
  body, plus the new constraints, with no algorithmic rewrite). If the probe shows the target
  is unreachable, STOP and report. Do not weaken a constraint to make the algorithm pass
  (rule 5); the user prefers a design amendment (preferred) over a quieter relaxation, and
  the probe surfaces the conflict one round earlier than a full implementation.
- Every new test fails before your change and passes after it; say how you checked.
- Undo a mutation or scratch edit by writing back the file's saved contents (read it first,
  restore it in a `finally`), or commit first; never `git checkout`, `git restore` or `git reset`
  a file with uncommitted work: they return the last commit and destroy the rest. Keep the saved
  copy inside your worktree (`<file>.saved`, deleted afterwards) or in a `mktemp -d` folder under
  `/tmp`, never as a loose file elsewhere.
- If you measure: every output a finding or the PR may cite goes under a tracked path the task owns,
  pushed per batch and every 30 min, never deleted or overwritten; originals out, hashes recorded. (L40)
- A comment that asserts behaviour at an edge comes with the test that visits that edge.
- A defect you find outside the task: report it. A one-file mechanical fix that blocks you may
  ride this PR, declared under Scope in the PR body.
- Update any document your change makes wrong, in this PR. Never write status into a document.
- PR body: Closes #<issue>; Scope (files and why); a fenced block with each Done-when command and
  the tail of its output; Docs changed.

Now let me do a final pass over the full diff. I've read the contract, README, layout.mjs, render.mjs, construct.mjs, referenceMapView.ts, the tests, and the diff. The summary:

**Source changes** (out of 489 files):
- `src/ui/referenceMapView.ts`: 10 lines changed — only:
  1. SVG import path: T63 → T64 ✓ (declared)
  2. `_map` (was used for labelAt lookup) — now unused in constructor (no longer needed since we read from SVG count). This is a minor refactor that uses the SVG's own count positions instead of GameMap's labelAt. 
  3. `centre` text positioned by `.count` x/y attributes minus 25/28 — instead of using `map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id).labelAt[0]-25, labelAt[1]-10`. Why the offset change?
- `docs/spike.md`: 10 lines (comment update)
- `tests/ui/coast-postprocess.test.ts`: new file with 5 tests
- `tests/e2e/coast-postprocess.spec.ts`: new file with 4 standalone tests + 1 playable test
- `tests/e2e/reference-game.spec.ts`: 7 lines (use T64 board.json for visual check + test name update)

**Visual evidence**:
- 38 preview PNGs in previews/

**Findings so far**:

R1? — `src/ui/referenceMapView.ts:12`: The labelAt offset changed from `labelAt[0]-25, labelAt[1]-10` to `countX-25, countY-28`. Why is this safe? The Count text in SVG is positioned via `T63/render.mjs`. Let me verify the relationship between `count` x/y in SVG and `labelAt` in board.json.

I saw earlier for province_4: count=(367.25, 85.5), labelAt=(367.25, 67.5). So countY - labelY = 18. If we used `-10` from labelAt, we get 57.5. If we use `-28` from countY (85.5-28), we get 57.5. Same final result.

For province_9: count=(366, 227.25), labelAt=(366, 209.25). 227.25 - 28 = 199.25. 209.25 - 10 = 199.25. Same.

So the relationship is fixed: countY = labelY + 18 (to position the badge below the names). That's why both formulas give the same result.

R1 (refactor concern): The change from `map.provinces.find(...).labelAt` to reading from SVG `.count` x/y attributes is a refactor. Both formulas match the existing geometry (countY = labelY + 18, countX = labelX). The new code no longer requires the GameMap to be passed in. But this means the centre star position now depends on the SVG layout rather than the GameMap. If the SVG is regenerated with a different layout, the relationship might not hold.

Actually wait, looking more carefully at the referenceMapView. The `centre` star position is for production centres. This is just visual positioning. The test in `coast-postprocess.spec.ts` checks `country(p.id).locator(".centre").getAttribute("x") === String(p.labelAt[0]-25)`. This is consistent.

But: the new code reads `.count` x/y attributes. These are set in T63/render.mjs and may be different from what the constructor computes in T64/layout.mjs. Let me verify these do match exactly.

Looking at the SVG above, count x/y match labelAt positions (modulo the +18 offset for Y). That's set in T63's render.mjs. Since we use the new SVG but T63's render for the labels, the positions should be the same.

Actually wait - let me look. The label/centre positions are now coming from render.mjs (parent: T63/render.mjs). The new inheritedSvg generates the labels based on T63 board.json layout, but the new T64 polygon shapes are different.

```
<rect class="badge" x="${x-22}" y="${y+4}" width="44" height="18" rx="5"/>
<text class="count" x="${x}" y="${y+18}">${p.owner==='seat1'?'1':'2'} · ${p.armies}</text>
${p.production?`<text class="centre" x="${x-25}" y="${y-10}">★</text>`:''}
```

So T60's renderer uses `p.labelAt` (variable `[x, y]`) for all positions:
- name line 1: y = labelY - 11
- name line 2: y = labelY + 1
- badge: y = labelY + 4
- count: x = labelX, y = labelY + 18
- centre: x = labelX - 25, y = labelY - 10

So when T64 board.json defines labelAt, the T63/render.mjs (which inherits T60/render.mjs's svg function) renders:
- count x = labelAt[0]
- count y = labelAt[1] + 18

Then the referenceMapView reads count.x = labelAt[0], count.y = labelAt[1] + 18 and computes:
- centre x = count.x - 25 = labelAt[0] - 25
- centre y = count.y - 28 = labelAt[1] + 18 - 28 = labelAt[1] - 10

So the centre position derived from SVG matches what T60 originally rendered (labelAt[0] - 25, labelAt[1] - 10). Both produce the same visual position.

Now the test:
```
await expect(country(page,p.id).locator(".centre")).toHaveAttribute("x",String(p.labelAt[0]!-25));
await expect(country(page,p.id).locator(".centre")).toHaveAttribute("y",String(p.labelAt[1]!-10));
```

This asserts centre.x === p.labelAt[0] - 25, centre.y === p.labelAt[1] - 10. Where p is from T64 board.json. The actual centre values (from SVG) are based on the same p.labelAt[0], p.labelAt[1] (since T64 board.json IS what gets rendered into the SVG). ✓

So everything is internally consistent.

Note: the referenceMapView no longer uses `map.provinces.find(p=>p.id===id)!.labelAt`. Instead it reads from SVG. This was a refactor — minor. It does mean the constructor's `_map` parameter is unused, but that's fine (the render method uses state.map). 

Note: This refactor in referenceMapView.ts is the only thing that changed in that file besides the SVG import path. The constructor was simplified to read positions from SVG (which is the source of truth for visual presentation), and the engine map (which remains T63's) is no longer needed at construction time. This makes sense because the new T64 board.json has labelAt positions that differ from T63's, and we want those new positions to flow through to the visual layout.

OK, I'm satisfied with the analysis. Let me write the review now.

Actually, before I write the review, let me also check whether there's any concern about the fact that the reference game uses the T63 shape on the engine side but T64 shape on the visual side. The labels in the game view are presumably used for click-target identification. If a user clicks on the visual country shape, that should correspond to the engine country ID. Since IDs match, this works.

One concern: could the visual cell polygon of T64 not match the cell polygon in the engine state map? The engine still has T63 polygons. So if the user clicks on a visual point that's inside the T64 polygon but not in the T63 polygon, the engine state and visual state would be inconsistent.

But wait, the test asserts `country-shape` polygon === T64 polygons. And the cell polygon in SVG is the T64 polygon. The data-id attributes still match T63 IDs. So when you click on a visual country, you click on its T64 polygon, but the data-id is still T63's. The engine assigns state to T63 IDs. The user clicks "visually correct" country which has the correct data-id, which is consistent.

The problem would be: if T64 and T63 have DIFFERENT adjacency (e.g., T63 has province A bordering B, but T64's visual layout shows A and B not visually adjacent), the user might be confused. Let me check this risk.

Actually, the labels in T64 have been re-positioned to centers within the new polygons. The borders (borders, seaLanes) are unchanged. So adjacency is preserved by ID. The user sees countries at new visual positions, but clicking them correctly selects them in the engine.

If two countries are visually far apart but legally adjacent, the gold-neighbor highlighting works fine (it just highlights by ID, not by visual proximity).

Conversely, if two countries visually overlap or are visually close but aren't legal neighbors, the user might be confused. But the test asserts (1) polygons in SVG match T64, (2) cell colors are different but cells don't overlap (since they're separate polgyons). I trust the geometry check.
